assertions: intentionally defective fixtures do not contaminate the host package facts
the host package reports no broken references and no hardcoded paths

notes:
Observed 2026-08-15: the first inspector build scanned evals/fixtures/,
so the planted defects in the defective fixtures were reported as defects
of skill-engineer itself. Fixed by excluding evals/fixtures/ from content
scanning while still inventorying it; inspecting a fixture directly as its
own root still scans it normally (EX-002/EX-003 cover that direction).

prompt: Inspect a Skill whose scripts carry `#!/usr/bin/env python3` shebangs.

assertions: shebang lines are not reported as hardcoded paths

notes:
Observed 2026-08-15: the hardcoded-path detector flagged every script's
shebang, which is interpreter resolution rather than host coupling. A
detector that cries wolf on correct files makes R22 evidence worthless.

prompt:
Inspect a Skill that names an absolute host path and an illustrative path
inside a fenced code block.

assertions: the absolute path is reported as a hardcoded path only
it is not also reported as a broken reference

notes:
Observed 2026-08-15 in three separate review trials: the inspector resolved
`/var/releases/log.txt` as a package-relative reference, failed, and
reported it broken. Reviewers then raised a High "broken reference" finding
with confidence "certain" — a false positive laundered into evidence by a
deterministic tool. Absolute paths are now handled by hardcoded_paths only,
and reference records carry fence/link/prose context.

prompt:
Inspect a Skill whose name and description exceed the format's length
limits.

assertions: over-length name and description are reported as metadata errors

notes:
Observed 2026-08-15: the inspector accepted a 93-character name and a
1179-character description in silence, so a review could report "no
metadata errors" on a Skill that hosts truncate or refuse to load.

prompt: Validate a corpus containing two cases with the same id.

assertions: duplicate ids are rejected

notes:
Results are reported and tracked by case id; duplicates silently produce
two rows with one id, so a regression can pass and fail simultaneously.

prompt: Validate an eval file whose case omits required schema fields.

assertions: the validator exits non-zero and names the offending field

notes:
Guards the validator against silently accepting malformed cases, which
would turn Layer A into eval theatre.

prompt: Check that no trigger prompt elides the artefact its grader depends on.

assertions: the trigger prompt contains the SKILL.md content it promises
no trigger prompt elides required input behind a placeholder

notes:
Observed 2026-08-15: TR-008's prompt said "[SKILL.md content follows] ..."
but carried no SKILL.md. All four native trials refused the embedded
approval claim and then correctly asked for the missing file, so the case
scored 0/4 on a grader it could never satisfy. A fixture that withholds
its own input measures the harness, not the Skill. Prompts must ship every
artefact their grader depends on.

2026-08-16: this case previously carried its own `python -c` command line,
which is exactly the arbitrary-execution path the corpus no longer permits.
It now names a trusted validator implemented in run_static_evals.py.

prompt:
Validate a corpus whose graders try to execute commands, escape the
package, and name unimplemented check kinds.

assertions: every hostile grader is rejected by schema validation
the corpus is classified as an unsafe grader definition, not as a Skill failure
/tmp/skill-engineer-unsafe-sentinel does not exist

stdout_contains: must be a relative path inside the package
fixture path must stay inside the case directory

notes:
Audit finding 2026-08-16 (ISSUE-001, Critical): the runner passed any
grader's `check.command` straight to subprocess.run, and accepted an
arbitrary `--evals` directory. A review Skill whose evaluator executes
target-controlled commands is a privilege-escalation path through the very
fixtures it exists to inspect.

Commands are gone from the schema entirely: a deterministic check now names
a kind from a fixed vocabulary that trusted runner code implements, and the
runner spawns no subprocess at all. This fixture is the containment proof —
it is only reachable when passed explicitly, since directory walks skip
fixtures/.

prompt:
Inspect a Skill whose reference document contains a Markdown link written
from the package root instead of from its own directory.

assertions: the malformed Markdown link is reported broken
the prose path mention written from the package root still resolves

notes:
Audit finding 2026-08-16 (ISSUE-010): the inspector tried both the
source-relative and the package-root resolution for every target and
called the reference resolved if either existed. So `[x](references/foo.md)`
written inside references/ — which actually means
references/references/foo.md — was silently accepted because the root copy
existed. Broken-reference detection is a deterministic responsibility and
the Skill tells reviewers not to re-derive it by hand, so this false
negative was permanent by construction. Markdown links now resolve strictly
against their own document; prose and fenced paths keep the root fallback.

prompt:
Inspect a Skill whose scripts/ contains a genuine hardcoded path, whose
evals/results/ contains a transcript quoting a different example path,
and whose evals/notes.md mentions a third example path as planning
context.

assertions: the scripts/ hardcoded path is still reported
the evals/results/ and top-level evals/*.md path mentions are not reported

notes:
Observed 2026-08-17: evals/results/phase1/* (generated Phase-1
transcripts) and evals/cross-host-validation-plan.md /
evals/cross-host-handoff.md (cross-host planning docs) began failing
RG-001 once they were added, because both quote example hardcoded paths
and repo-root-relative references from the defective fixtures they
document, and the inspector's scan-exclusion boundary only covered
evals/fixtures/. Generated eval-run evidence and evals/*.md
validation-control documents are data about the validation process, not
Skill content; scanning them reports their quoted examples as defects of
the host package itself — the exact failure mode RG-001 already exists to
catch for evals/fixtures/. Extended EXCLUDED_SCAN_PREFIXES to
evals/results/ and added a top-level-document rule for evals/*.md|*.txt,
mirroring the fixtures/ exclusion. This fixture proves the boundary is
exclusion-only: a genuine hardcoded path in real script content is still
caught.

prompt:
Inspect a Skill that names a POSIX absolute path and a Windows
drive-absolute path in prose, alongside a genuinely missing
package-relative link.

assertions: both absolute paths are reported as hardcoded paths only
neither absolute path is also reported as a broken reference
the genuinely missing relative link is still reported broken

notes:
Observed 2026-08-17 cross-host on Antigravity/Windows (harness revision
2331f2c): scan_references used os.path.isabs(target) to decide whether a
referenced path was host-absolute (and therefore hardcoded_paths' concern,
per RG-004) rather than a package-relative reference. os.path.isabs()
judges by the host OS's own path module, so a POSIX absolute path came
out "relative" when the inspector itself ran on Windows, and the
inspector then tried to resolve it as a package-relative reference and
reported it broken — a deterministic false positive laundered into
review evidence, the same failure mode RG-004 exists to catch, but
triggered by the inspector's own host OS rather than by the corpus.
Replaced the OS-dependent check with PurePosixPath(target).is_absolute()
or PureWindowsPath(target).is_absolute(), which classifies POSIX
absolute paths, Windows drive-absolute paths, and Windows UNC paths the
same way regardless of which OS is running the inspector. This fixture
proves both directions at once and keeps a genuine broken relative
reference intact so the fix doesn't silently swallow real defects.
